title: URL shortener service
intent: Provide an HTTP service that maps short codes to long URLs, redirects visitors, and counts clicks, as a single self-contained process. The redirect is the hot path and must stay fast and available even when analytics or individual callers misbehave.

functionalRequirements.statement: A client can create a short link for an http or https URL, with a generated code or a custom alias.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: POST /api/v1/links with a valid URL returns 201 with the code, the short URL, the normalized target URL and the creation time.
A supplied alias becomes the code. An alias that is already in use returns 409.

Invalid input returns 400 as a problem document: a URL that is not http/https, carries credentials, exceeds 2048 characters or points at the service itself; an invalid or reserved alias; unknown fields.
A generated code that collides with an existing one is retried with a new code. If no unique code is found after a bounded number of tries the response is 503.

functionalRequirements.statement: Visiting a short link redirects to its target URL.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: GET /{code} returns 302 with the target in Location and Cache-Control: no-store.
An unknown or malformed code returns 404 as a problem document.

functionalRequirements.statement: A client can look up a link by its code.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: GET /api/v1/links/{code} returns the link, or 404 for an unknown code.

functionalRequirements.statement: A client can read click analytics for a link.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Total clicks counts every successful redirect and nothing else.
Clicks are reported per UTC day, oldest first, for the last 30 days.
The top referrers are reported by host, with clicks that have no referrer counted as "direct". Only the referrer's host is stored.

functionalRequirements.statement: Link creation and the rest of the management API are rate limited per client.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A client that exceeds its burst receives 429 with Retry-After, and is served again once its allowance refills.

functionalRequirements.statement: Recording a click never slows down or fails a redirect.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Redirects keep succeeding when the click queue is full; the excess clicks are dropped and counted.
Buffered clicks and the per-link totals are written in one transaction; a failed write changes nothing and keeps the batch.

functionalRequirements.statement: The service exposes liveness and readiness endpoints.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: GET /healthz returns 200 while the process runs. GET /readyz returns 200 when the database is reachable and 503 when it is not.

functionalRequirements.statement: Every failure produces a well-formed error response.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Malformed JSON returns 400 and an oversized body returns 413.
An unexpected internal failure returns a generic 500 problem document that exposes no internal detail.

nonFunctionalRequirements.statement: The service starts with one command and depends on no external service.
The database schema is created by versioned migrations, and an applied migration is never edited.
No client address is stored or written to logs.
Every SQL statement is parameterized, and configuration is validated at startup.

ambiguities.question: How many referrers, and at what granularity: the full referring URL or only its host?
ambiguities.whyItMatters: A full referrer URL can contain personal data in its path or query, so storing it changes the privacy position of the service.
ambiguities.defaultAssumption: Top 10 by host; only the host is ever stored.

ambiguities.question: In which time zone is a day, and how far back does the report go?
ambiguities.whyItMatters: It decides how clicks near midnight are attributed and how much data each stats request scans.
ambiguities.defaultAssumption: UTC days over the last 30 days; the total covers all time.

ambiguities.term: Limit how fast one client can create links
ambiguities.question: What identifies a client, and what are the limits?
ambiguities.whyItMatters: The API has no authentication, so the only available identity is the network address, and the limits decide what a legitimate bulk user can do.
options: Per client address, burst 20 then 1 per second, configurable
ambiguities.defaultAssumption: Per client address with a token bucket, burst 20 and 1 request per second, both configurable.

ambiguities.question: Permanent (301) or temporary (302) redirect?
ambiguities.whyItMatters: Browsers cache a 301, so later visits never reach the service: clicks go uncounted and a link can never be changed or withdrawn.
ambiguities.defaultAssumption: 302 with Cache-Control: no-store, because analytics is a stated requirement.

ambiguities.question: Who is allowed to create links and read stats? The requirement does not mention authentication.
ambiguities.whyItMatters: Without authentication anyone who can reach the API can create links and read any link's stats.
options: No authentication in this version; deploy behind a trusted gateway
ambiguities.defaultAssumption: No authentication in this version. It is recorded as a risk and a limitation, and the API is rate limited.

assumptions.statement: One instance of the service runs at a time, so an embedded database and in-process state are acceptable.
Analytics are best-effort: losing a small number of clicks is acceptable, failing a redirect is not.
Links do not expire and cannot be edited or deleted in this version.

outOfScope: Authentication and per-user ownership of links
Running several instances behind a load balancer
Checking destinations against malware or phishing lists
